trading_type: Swing Trading, Smart Money Concepts (SMC), Risk Management
cleaned_caption:
How to mark a chart before you enter a trade: trend, support, resistance, swing, liquidity and entry zone 📊

Most traders don’t lose because of a bad strategy. They lose because they enter on an unmarked chart and guess.

This is the chart reading checklist I use before every entry:

1. Trend: higher highs and higher lows, or lower highs and lower lows

2. Support: the floor where buyers stepped in before

3. Resistance: the ceiling where sellers pushed price back

4. Swing high and swing low: where your stop loss and first target come from

5. Liquidity: equal lows where stops pile up and price sweeps first

6. Entry zone: trend + level + reaction, with risk reward planned before you click

title: Trading consistency comes from mastering one trading strategy, no
trading_type: Quantitative & Algorithmic, Trading Psychology, Risk Management
cleaned_caption:
Trading consistency comes from mastering one trading strategy, not switching between many. 📈

Many traders jump from strategy to strategy: a new indicator, a new setup, a new YouTube system. Every losing week feels like proof the strategy failed, so they start over again. But no trading strategy wins every week. 🔁

Focus is a real edge in trading. When you stick to one setup, you learn how it behaves in trending and ranging markets, how to manage risk with it, and when to stay out. That depth builds confidence, discipline and consistent results. 🎯

Backtest it. Journal every trade. Give it time before you judge it.
